title: Without Food, Bigger People Last Longer 🏝️
short_title: Without Food, Bigger People Last Longer 🏝️
title_options: Without Food, Bigger People Last Longer 🏝️
One Man Didn't Eat for 382 Days 😳
Body Fat Is Your Backup Food Tank 😳
seo_intro:
How long can you survive without food? With water, a bigger person usually lasts longer: body fat is stored energy, and one pound holds about 3,500 calories.
The body also burns muscle, even the heart. Angus Barbieri fasted 382 days under medical supervision in Scotland (1965–66) and lost 276 pounds.
sources_text: Stewart W.K. & Fleming L.W., "Features of a successful therapeutic fast of 382 days' duration", Postgraduate Medical Journal, 1973 (Angus Barbieri, Dundee, 1965–66: 456 to 180 lb); Keys A. et al., The Biology of Human Starvation (Minnesota Starvation Experiment), 1950 (loss of muscle mass and heart size during starvation); Wishnofsky M., "Caloric equivalents of gained or lost weight", American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 1958 (about 3,500 calories per pound of body fat, an approximation)
disclaimer: Original illustrations (simplified). Synthetic voice and AI-generated music. Not medical advice: never fast without a doctor.
